sections.h2: Who in Carrollton collects the tax and who values the house?
sections.html:
The Carroll County Tax Commissioner, at 423 College Street, Room 401, collects. Call 770-830-5843 for bill questions or 770-830-5826 for the tag and tax counter. Counter service runs weekdays from 8 to 5, and title transactions end at 4:30.

Valuation sits with the Board of Tax Assessors at 770-830-5812. In Carroll County the assessors also take property tax returns and homestead applications, which differs from counties where the commissioner does. The commissioner's office states that it does not assess property or set millage, and that the county commissioners and the school board levy the rates.

  • Late interest, returned mail, a bill total: tax commissioner.
  • Value, exemption, return or appeal: assessors.
  • Copy of your warranty deed: Clerk of Superior Court, in the courthouse.

Card payments, whether at the counter or on the commissioner's site, add a 2.5% fee kept by the payment processor Assurance.

sections.h2: What is the December 1 deadline in Carroll County?
sections.html:
December 1 is the usual due date for real estate and business personal property. The commissioner's FAQ says the date was December 21 until the county commissioners signed a resolution in December 2009 moving it. Manufactured homes pay by April 1, and vehicle tax follows the owner's birthday.

A mailed check counts on a United States Postal Service postmark, but a postage-meter stamp does not. Statements go to the owner and never to a mortgage company, so an escrow borrower has to hand theirs over.

Interest then accrues each month at the bank prime loan rate plus 3%. Any tax unpaid 120 days after the deadline draws a 5% penalty, repeated every 120 days until it totals 20%, with an exemption for homestead accounts under $500.

sections.h2: Why settle a Carroll County lien before listing?
sections.html:
After 120 days past due, the commissioner may record a tax FiFa with the Clerk of Superior Court. The office warns that the entry is public and credit bureaus can read it, and that it has no say in how they use it. If the tax stays unpaid, the commissioner can levy on the house, which the office describes as a last resort.

Carroll's tax sale page names the next auction date and says bidders must show up with cash, certified funds or a bank letter. Neither step has to happen to your house. A title company can obtain a payoff from the commissioner, print it on the settlement statement and pay the county out of your proceeds, so the lien never reaches the courthouse steps.

sections.h2: What are the Carroll County appeal rules and choices?
sections.html:
Notices of assessment must be mailed by July 1. The appeal is due in writing within 45 days of the notice date, and the right is gone afterward. The notice shows fair market value, assessed value and a tax estimate built on last year's millage.

At filing you choose one of three tracks: the Board of Equalization with a further appeal to Superior Court; arbitration with no Superior Court appeal; or, for non-homestead parcels worth more than $1 million, a hearing officer with Superior Court appeal rights.

  • Allowed grounds: taxability, value, uniformity with similar parcels.
  • Not allowed: a complaint that the levy itself is too high.
  • Math: tax equals fair market value times 40%, less exemptions, times the millage rate.

sections.h2: Which Carroll County relief programs end when the house sells?
sections.html:
Homestead applications go to the assessors and must be filed before April 1 to cover that year. A first-time filer brings the warranty deed. The exemption renews on its own until the owner moves or title changes.

The commissioner's general information page describes an elderly school tax exemption for owners 62 and older whose net income is at most $10,000, a general exemption for owners 65 and older under the same cap, and a deferral program for owners 62 and older with household income of $15,000 or less. Deferred tax stays on the property until ownership changes or it hits 85% of fair market value, so a sale makes it payable.

Farmland assessed at 30% of fair market value, and conservation-use land assessed at its current use, both rest on a covenant with the assessors to hold the use for 10 years. Ask the assessors what a sale does to that covenant before you list acreage that carries one.

sections.h2: Does Carroll County offer other special assessments beyond homestead?
sections.html:
Yes, a handful, and each one carries conditions that can matter to a buyer. Historic property listed on the Georgia or National Register of Historic Places may get a preferential assessment covering the building and up to two acres around it, once the Department of Natural Resources certifies it as rehabilitated or landmark historic property.

Brownfield property in the state's Hazardous Site Reuse and Redevelopment Program can have its taxable assessment effectively frozen for ten years while a developer cleans it up. Forest land conservation use has a 15-year covenant and is limited to tracts above 200 acres, and the residence on the land is excluded from the break.

  • Mobile homes: the owner files a return and gets a location permit, and the current year's tax must be paid in full first.
  • Returns for real and personal property are filed January 1 through April 1 with the assessors.
  • A new return can state a different value, which preserves your appeal rights if the board changes the number again.

sections.h2: How did Carroll County grow into a 130,000-resident county?
sections.html:
Carroll lies on the Alabama line in west Georgia, with 499 square miles of land. Lines were drawn on June 9, 1825, and the county was named in 1826 for Charles Carroll of Carrollton. In the 1850s it was nicknamed the Free State of Carroll, and it saw Georgia's first gold rush. The 2020 census counted 119,148 residents and the 2025 estimate is 131,036.

Carrollton is the seat and biggest city. Villa Rica (half of it in Douglas County), Temple, Bowdon, Mount Zion, Whitesburg and Roopville complete the list of municipalities. Interstate 20 crosses the north, joined by U.S. 27, U.S. 78 and State Routes 5, 16, 61, 100, 101, 113, 166 and 274. Carroll has three school districts, and the Carrollton Greenbelt is a local walking and cycling route.

Weather has left a mark: tornadoes hit in February and May 2008, and flooding in September 2009 closed more than 60 roads and wrecked bridges. Buyers of older homes sometimes ask about storm repairs.

faqs.q: When do Carroll County property taxes come due?
faqs.a: December 1 for real estate and business personal property, under a resolution the county commissioners adopted in December 2009. Manufactured homes are due April 1. Read the date on your statement to be sure.

faqs.q: What does lateness add to a Carroll County bill?
faqs.a: Monthly interest at the bank prime loan rate plus 3%, and a 5% penalty that starts at 120 days and repeats every 120 days to a 20% ceiling. Homestead accounts under $500 are spared the penalty.

faqs.q: Is there a fee for card payment in Carroll County?
faqs.a: Yes, 2.5%, collected by the payment processor, whether you pay at the counter or online. The county itself does not receive it. Ask the commissioner's office about other payment methods.

faqs.q: Does the Carroll County Tax Commissioner set my tax?
faqs.a: No. The commissioner bills what the assessors' values and the millage rates produce, and the rates come from the county commissioners and the school board. Value questions go to 770-830-5812.

faqs.q: What is the Carroll County homestead cutoff?
faqs.a: April 1. File with the Tax Assessor's Office at 423 College Street. A late application waits for the next tax year, and first-time applicants should bring their warranty deed.
